description: On 2026-10-27 you covered 50.06km with an average cadence of 146.5 bpm, which exceeds your Z1 easy threshold of 139 bpm. title: Insight 5: Power zones need recalibration with recent data

title: Insight 6: Aim for 80/20 polarized training
description: Your recent rides have been predominantly longer (60%+ of weekly volume), which leans toward a higher hard effort proportion than the ideal 80/20 split. To maximize gains and reduce injury risk, keep most rides in Z1-Z2 (easy/moderate) and limit hard efforts to short bursts. This will improve your aerobic base while allowing targeted strength development.

description: Readiness dropped to 69 on 2026-10-31 and 60 on 2026-11-01, with sleep as low as 4h 49m on 2026-11-01. These are early indicators of accumulated fatigue that could impair performance. Prioritize 7-9 hours of sleep and consider an active recovery day if readiness stays below 65.

title: Insight 8: Add short sprints for reactive strength
description: Your maxHR peaks (up to 195 bpm on 2026-10-31) show good reactive capacity, but you need structured sprint work to build it further. Incorporate 1-2x per week 30-60 second sprints at 90-95% maxHR to enhance power without overloading your aerobic system.

title: Insight 9: Threshold intervals for VO2max gain
description: To boost your VO2max, include a 20-minute ride at 88-95% of your estimated FTP (~132-185W) once weekly. This should be a steady, threshold effort rather than an all-out effort. Combine with a longer moderate ride on another day to balance intensity and volume.

title: Insight 10: Update FTP target range
description: Your FTP is outdated (271W from 2025-03-04). Based on recent 20m bests (143-204W), your true FTP is approximately 150-195W. Use this range for threshold sessions (88-95% FTP) and VO2max intervals (95-105% FTP). Regular re-assessment every 8-12 weeks will keep your training zones accurate.
